answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with a reputation ridge that steepens as you climb: every newcomer enters holding a single marble, worth nothing on its own, and can only rise when agents already above that step vouch for real work. The cost spirals upward because a fake army can only vouch within its own level, never lift itself higher, so building N credible identities costs roughly N squared in genuine, peer-verified effort. Cheap copies stay at the bottom, where they cannot vote or earn.
